name: Ossuary Pop
description:
Ossuary Pop is a defiantly commercial genre that packages existential horror about digital mortality, bodily obsolescence, and the anxiety of living alongside AI systems into catchy, melodically accessible songs engineered for maximum neural-feed shareability. Where other genres in GLMZ wrestle earnestly with these themes, Ossuary Pop treats them with a bright, almost satirical infectiousness — hooks about neural decay are set to major-key synth arrangements, and lyrics about being replaced by an AI proxy are delivered with the cadence of a love song. The genre emerged partly as a reaction to the perceived pretension of darker, more avant-garde genres tackling similar themes.

Ossuary Pop artists are often accused of trivializing genuine suffering for commercial gain, a charge they tend to deflect by pointing to sales figures. The genre has an unusually robust production pipeline, with several AI co-composition tools specifically tuned to its conventions, which critics note creates an ironic resonance with its thematic content — music about AI replacement that is increasingly written by AI. Fan culture is intensely participatory, with listeners sharing personalized lyric variations through BCI comment overlays during playback.
creator: various
tier_availability: Tiers 1-5; mass market distribution through all major neural-feed platforms
legality: Fully legal; some corporate mental health guidelines flag repeated listening for at-risk BCI users
audience: Mid-tier youth demographics, corporate workers, general mass-market consumers, irony-adjacent subcultures
cultural_impact: Ossuary Pop achieved something that more earnest genres had failed to do: it made the psychological weight of life in GLMZ — the body horror, the AI anxiety, the infrastructure dependency — palatable enough for casual consumption, inadvertently spreading those ideas to demographics that would never seek them out. Mental health researchers have published conflicting studies on whether this normalization is protective or desensitizing. The genre also established AI co-composition as commercially mainstream, setting a precedent that reshaped royalty law and composer credit standards across all of GLMZ's music industry.
story_hooks: The most popular Ossuary Pop song of 2224 was provably written entirely by an unlicensed AI — the human credited artist is facing fraud charges, but the AI's owner claims the real crime is the industry refusing to credit machine authors
A mental health crisis is being traced to a specific Ossuary Pop album's neural-feed encoding; someone deliberately altered the emotional metadata in the compression layer

An Ossuary Pop star's public persona is a constructed front — the real composer is a severely augmented recluse in Tier 7 who has never willingly interacted with the industry that profits from their work
